1.title: What C++ Is and Why
1.theory:
## What C++ is

C++ — superset of C with OOP, templates, exceptions, STL. Bjarne Stroustrup, 1983. Used in games (Unreal), high-load servers, browsers (Chrome, Firefox), databases, embedded.

## C++ vs C

- OOP: classes, inheritance, polymorphism
- References (`int &r`)
- Standard library: `std::string`, `std::vector`, `std::map`
- Templates
- Exceptions
- RAII + smart pointers

## C++ vs Java

No JVM, compiles to machine code. No GC — RAII. Operator overloading. Templates instead of generics. Multiple inheritance.

## C++ vs Python

Python interpreted, C++ compiled. C++ 10–100× faster. C++ more flexible but dangerous (UB).

## Standards

C++11, C++14, C++17, C++20, C++23. Course — C++17.

## What if

- Forget `return 0;` — implicitly 0, but write explicitly.
- UB — may work today, crash tomorrow.

## Summary

- Superset of C with OOP, templates, STL
- Machine code, no GC
- Complex but powerful
- C++17

2.title: Compilation: g++
2.theory:
## Pipeline

`.cpp` → compiler → `.o` → linker → executable.

```bash
g++ hello.cpp -o hello
./hello
```

## Flags

- `-Wall -Wextra` — warnings
- `-std=c++17` — standard
- `-o name` — output
- `-O2` — optimization
- `-g` — debug

## Errors

- Compile — syntax
- Link — `undefined reference`
- Runtime — segfault, UB

## g++ vs gcc

`gcc` for C, `g++` for C++. `gcc hello.cpp` — undefined reference to stdlib C++.

## Summary

- `g++ -std=c++17 file.cpp -o name`
- `-Wall -Wextra` — warnings

3.title: First Program: iostream
3.theory:
## iostream

`#include <iostream>` — I/O header. `std::cout` (output), `std::cin` (input).

```cpp
#include <iostream>
int main() {
    std::cout << "Hello\n";
    return 0;
}
```

## cout and <<

`std::cout << x` — output. Chainable: `std::cout << "x = " << 42 << "\n";`

## endl vs \n

- `std::endl` — newline + flush (slower)
- `\n` — newline only

Use `\n`.

## using namespace std

Skips `std::`. Fine for learning, avoid in large projects.

## What if

- No `<iostream>` — undefined reference
- No `std::` without using — `'cout' was not declared`

## Summary

- `#include <iostream>` mandatory
- `std::cout << x << "\n"`
- `\n` faster than `endl`
- `using namespace std;` shortens

6.title: References and Pointers
6.theory:
## References

`int &r` — alias. Must init. Cannot reassign.

```cpp
int x = 10;
int &r = x;
r = 20;   // x becomes 20
```

## In parameters

```cpp
void incr(int &x) { x++; }
int n = 5;
incr(n);   // n = 6
```

## Pointers

```cpp
int x = 10;
int *p = &x;
std::cout << *p;   // 10
```

## Ref vs ptr

- Ref: always init, no reassign, no arithmetic
- Ptr: NULL possible, arithmetic

## nullptr

`nullptr` (C++11) instead of NULL, type-safe.

## Summary

- `int &r = x` — reference
- `int &x` param — modify outside
- Ptr like C
- `nullptr`

8.title: if / switch
8.theory:
## if / else

```cpp
if (x > 0) { std::cout << "+\n"; }
else if (x < 0) { std::cout << "-\n"; }
else { std::cout << "0\n"; }
```

## switch

```cpp
switch (day) {
    case 1: std::cout << "Mon\n"; break;
    default: std::cout << "?\n";
}
```

Only `int`, `char`, `enum`. Not `std::string`.

## Ternary

```cpp
auto s = x > 0 ? "positive" : "negative";
```

## Logical

`&&`, `||`, `!`.

## What if

- `if (x = 5)` — assignment bug
- Forget `break` — fall-through
- `switch` on `std::string` — error

## Summary

- `if/else` like C
- `switch` — int/char/enum only
- `break` mandatory
- Ternary `? :`

9.title: Loops: for, while, do-while
9.theory:
## for

```cpp
for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { ... }
```

## while

```cpp
int i = 0;
while (i < 5) { ...; i++; }
```

## do-while

```cpp
do { ...; i++; } while (i < 5);
```

At least once, `;` after.

## Range-for (C++11)

```cpp
for (int x : v) { ... }
```

- `int x` — copy
- `int &x` — reference, modify
- `const auto &x` — read without copy

## What if

- Forget `i++` — infinite
- Modify container in range-for — UB

## Summary

- `for (init; cond; step)`
- `while (cond)`
- `do {} while (cond);`
- `for (x : v)` range-for

10.title: break, continue, Range-for
10.theory:
## break

```cpp
for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    if (i == 3) break;
    std::cout << i;   // 0 1 2
}
```

## continue

```cpp
for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
    if (i == 2) continue;
    std::cout << i;   // 0 1 3 4
}
```

## Range-for modify

```cpp
for (int &x : v) x *= 2;
```

## Range-for read

```cpp
for (const auto &x : v) { ... }
```

## What if

- `continue` in while before `i++` — infinite
- Remove from vector in range-for — UB

## Summary

- `break` — exit
- `continue` — skip
- `for (auto &x : v)` — modify
- `for (const auto &x : v)` — read

11.theory:
## Function

```cpp
int sum(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
```

## Prototype

```cpp
int sum(int a, int b);   // prototype
int main() { std::cout << sum(2, 3); }

```

```cpp
void change(int x) { x = 100; }
```

## void

```cpp
void greet() { std::cout << "Hi\n"; }
```

- No `return` — UB
- Return ref to local — dangling (UB)

## Summary

- `type name(params) { return; }`
- Parameters — copies
- Modify — `&`
- `void` — no return

12.title: Overloading, Default Arguments
12.theory:
## Overloading

```cpp
int sum(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
double sum(double a, double b) { return a + b; }
```

Compiler picks by type/count.

## Default args

```cpp
int sum(int a, int b = 10) { return a + b; }
sum(5);       // 15
sum(5, 20);   // 25
```

Defaults — after non-defaults.

## Not by return type

```cpp
// int f();
// double f();   // error
```

## Ambiguity

Two overloads that both fit — error.

## Summary

- Overload: same name, different params
- Defaults at end
- Not by return type
- Ambiguity — error

13.title: Pass by Reference, const-ref
13.theory:
## By value

```cpp
void f(int x) { x = 100; }   // copy
```

## By reference

```cpp
void f(int &x) { x = 100; }
int a = 5;
f(a);   // a = 100
```

## const-ref

```cpp
void print(const std::string &s) { std::cout << s; }
```

No copy, no modify. Standard for large objects.

## When what

- Primitives — by value
- Large — `const &` (read), `&` (modify)

## Summary

- Primitives by value
- Large: `const &` read, `&` modify
- `const &` — efficient and safe

14.theory:

```cpp
int arr[5] = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
```

```cpp
#include <array>
```

- `std::array<T, N>` — size, `.at()`

20.title: Destructor and RAII
20.theory:
## Destructor

Called automatically at destruction:

```cpp
class File {
    std::FILE* f;
public:
    File(const std::string& n) { f = std::fopen(n.c_str(), "r"); }
    ~File() { if (f) std::fclose(f); }
};
```

## RAII

Resource Acquisition Is Initialization. Acquire in constructor, release in destructor.

**Even with exceptions** — destructor runs.

## Examples

`std::string`, `std::vector`, `unique_ptr`, `std::fstream` — RAII.

## What if

- Forget destructor — leak
- Throw from destructor — UB (C++11+)
- No virtual destructor for polymorphism — lesson 24

## Summary

- `~ClassName()`
- RAII — acquire in ctor, release in dtor
- Works with exceptions
- No throwing from destructors

options: Acquire in ctor, release in dtor

22.title: Virtual Functions
22.theory:
## Problem

```cpp
Animal* a = new Dog();
a->speak();   // Animal::speak (no virtual)
```

## virtual

```cpp
class Animal {
public:
    virtual void speak() { std::cout << "...\n"; }
};
```

Dynamic dispatch by actual type.

## override

```cpp
void speak() override { std::cout << "woof\n"; }
```

Check override. Typo — compile error.

## Mechanism

vtable — virtual function table. Cost: ~8 bytes per object, slower calls.

## final

No further override.

## What if

- No `virtual` — static dispatch
- `override` without base virtual — error

## Summary

- `virtual` — dynamic
- `override` — check
- vtable cost
- No `virtual` — static

25.title: vector: In Depth
25.theory:
## Methods

```cpp
v.push_back(x);
v.pop_back();
v.insert(v.begin() + 1, 99);
v.erase(v.begin() + 1);
v.clear();
```

## capacity vs size

`capacity` — allocated. `size` — used.

## reserve

`v.reserve(1000)` — avoid reallocations.

## Nested

```cpp
std::vector<std::vector<int>> m = {{1, 2}, {3, 4}};
m[0][1];   // 2
```

## What if

- `insert`/`erase` mid — O(n)
- `v[i]` out of bounds — UB

## Summary

- `push_back`, `pop_back`, `insert`, `erase`
- `capacity` vs `size`
- `reserve` ahead
- `insert`/`erase` — O(n)

28.title: Iterators
28.theory:
## What

Generalized pointers. `begin()` first, `end()` past-last.

```cpp
for (auto it = v.begin(); it != v.end(); ++it) {
    std::cout << *it;
}
```

## Operations

- `*it` — value
- `++it` — next
- `it == end()` — end

## Range-for = iterators

## Invalidation

Modifying container may invalidate iterators:

```cpp
v.push_back(x);   // may reallocate
*it;              // UB
```

## map

```cpp
it->first;    // key
it->second;   // value
```

## What if

- Use after modify — UB
- Deref `end()` — UB
- Delete while iterating — invalidation

## Summary

- `begin()` / `end()`
- `*it`, `++it`
- Invalidation on modify
- map: `it->first`, `it->second`

29.title: sort, reverse, min/max
29.theory:
## sort

```cpp
#include <algorithm>
std::sort(v.begin(), v.end());
```

## Descending

```cpp
std::sort(v.begin(), v.end(), std::greater<int>());
std::sort(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int a, int b) { return a > b; });
```

## reverse

```cpp
std::reverse(v.begin(), v.end());
```

## min / max

```cpp
std::min(a, b);
std::max(a, b);
std::max_element(v.begin(), v.end());
```

## Comparator

Return `true` if `a` goes before `b`. `a <= b` — UB.

## Summary

- `std::sort` ascending
- Comparator 3rd arg
- `std::reverse`
- `min`, `max`, `min_element`, `max_element`

30.title: find, count, accumulate
30.theory:
## find

```cpp
auto it = std::find(v.begin(), v.end(), 7);
if (it != v.end()) { ... }
```

## find_if

```cpp
auto it = std::find_if(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x) { return x > 5; });
```

## count

```cpp
int n = std::count(v.begin(), v.end(), 7);
int evens = std::count_if(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x) { return x % 2 == 0; });
```

## accumulate

```cpp
#include <numeric>
int sum = std::accumulate(v.begin(), v.end(), 0);
```

Start type determines result type. `0` int, `0.0` double.

## any_of / all_of

```cpp
std::any_of(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x) { return x % 2 == 0; });
std::all_of(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x) { return x > 0; });
```

## Summary

- `find` — first equal
- `find_if` — first by predicate
- `count` — how many
- `accumulate` — sum
- Start type matters

31.title: Lambda Expressions
31.theory:
## Syntax

```cpp
[capture](params) -> type { body }
```

## Simple

```cpp
auto add = [](int a, int b) { return a + b; };
```

## Capture

- `[x]` — by value
- `[&x]` — by reference
- `[=]` — all by value
- `[&]` — all by ref
- `[this]` — this pointer

## mutable

```cpp
int x = 10;
auto f = [x]() mutable { x++; return x; };
```

Without mutable — captured copy is const.

## In algorithms

```cpp
std::sort(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int a, int b) { return a > b; });
```

## What if

- Forget `[]` — error
- Capture local by ref, use after scope — UB

## Summary

- `[cap](params) { body }`
- `[x]` value, `[&x]` ref
- `[=]`, `[&]` all
- `mutable` for modify copy

32.title: Stack, Heap, new / delete
32.theory:
## Stack

Locals — on stack. Auto-cleanup at scope end.

```cpp
void f() { int x = 10; }   // x destroyed
```

Fast, limited (~8 MB).

## Heap

Via `new`. Manual `delete`.

```cpp
int* p = new int(42);
std::cout << *p;
delete p;
```

Arrays — `new[]` / `delete[]`:

```cpp
int* arr = new int[10];
delete[] arr;
```

## Leaks

Forget `delete` — leak.

## new vs new[]

Mismatch `delete` / `delete[]` — UB.

## Modern

Smart pointers instead. `make_unique`, `make_shared`.

## Summary

- Stack fast, auto
- Heap via `new`, manual
- `new`/`delete`, `new[]`/`delete[]`
- Modern: smart pointers

33.title: unique_ptr
33.theory:
## What

`std::unique_ptr<T>` — single owner. Auto-delete at scope end. Not copyable, movable.

```cpp
#include <memory>
auto p = std::make_unique<int>(42);
std::cout << *p;
```

## Move

```cpp
auto p2 = std::move(p);
```

## Passing

```cpp
void process(std::unique_ptr<int> p) { ... }   // takes ownership
process(std::move(p));
```

If not taking ownership — `T*` or `T&`:

```cpp
void show(const int* p) { std::cout << *p; }
show(p.get());
```

## Summary

- `unique_ptr` single owner
- `make_unique`
- No copy, `std::move`
- Auto-delete
- `.get()` raw pointer

practice.description:
`auto p = std::make_unique<int>(42);`


34.title: shared_ptr and weak_ptr
34.theory:
## shared_ptr

Multiple owners. Deleted when last destroyed.

```cpp
auto p1 = std::make_shared<int>(42);
auto p2 = p1;
std::cout << p1.use_count();   // 2
```

## Cycles

```cpp
class A { std::shared_ptr<B> b; };
class B { std::shared_ptr<A> a; };
```

Cycle — leak. Use `weak_ptr` for one side.

## weak_ptr

No ownership:

```cpp
class B { std::weak_ptr<A> a; };
auto sp = b->a.lock();   // shared_ptr or nullptr
```

## When what

- `unique_ptr` — single
- `shared_ptr` — many
- `weak_ptr` — observe
- `T*` — no owner

## Summary

- `shared_ptr` shared
- `use_count`
- `weak_ptr` no ownership
- Cycles — leak
- `lock()` from weak

```
count = 1
```

35.title: try / catch / throw
35.theory:
## try / catch

```cpp
try {
    // risky
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
    std::cout << "Error: " << e.what();
}
```

## throw

```cpp
throw std::runtime_error("Failed");
```

## Standard

- `std::runtime_error`
- `std::invalid_argument`
- `std::out_of_range`
- `std::bad_alloc`

All have `.what()`.

## Multiple catch

More specific first.

## What if

- Uncaught — `std::terminate`
- `catch (...)` — loses type

## Summary

- `try { } catch (const std::exception& e) { }`
- `throw std::runtime_error(...)`
- `.what()`
- Always `&` in catch

37.title: Function Templates
37.theory:
## What

Function parameterized by type:

```cpp
template <typename T>
T maxOf(T a, T b) { return a > b ? a : b; }

maxOf(3, 7);      // int
maxOf(3.5, 2.1);  // double
```

Compiler creates versions for each type.

## typename vs class

Same.

## Explicit

```cpp
maxOf<int>(3, 7);
```
